# Markdown [Exact GFM footnote round-trip]

`[^id]` and `[^id]: …` round-trip through
[`@lexical/mdast`](https://github.com/facebook/lexical). The extension teaches
mdast the GFM footnote grammar on both sides — parse and serialize — so a
document read from markdown and written back out comes back unchanged.

## Register the extension

`FootnoteMdastExtension` sits alongside the `@lexical/mdast` extensions; it adds
the footnote import/export rules and pulls in the core `FootnoteExtension`
itself.

```tsx twoslash
// @twoslash-cache: {"v":1,"hash":"de14d62291491ba64653518f9eaab2ca3a9df0b30d251dffa4e4220fbe6f26e5","data":""}
import {buildEditorFromExtensions} from '@lexical/extension';
import {
  MdastCommonMarkExtension,
  MdastExportExtension,
  MdastGfmExtension,
  MdastShortcutsExtension,
} from '@lexical/mdast';
import {RichTextExtension} from '@lexical/rich-text';
import {FootnoteExtension} from 'lexical-footnote';
import {FootnoteMdastExtension} from 'lexical-footnote/mdast';

const editor = buildEditorFromExtensions({
  dependencies: [
    RichTextExtension,
    MdastCommonMarkExtension,
    MdastGfmExtension,
    MdastShortcutsExtension,
    MdastExportExtension,
    FootnoteExtension,
    FootnoteMdastExtension,
  ],
  name: 'my-editor',
  namespace: 'my-app',
});
```

With it registered, the `@lexical/mdast` convert functions carry footnotes
through untouched:

```ts
import {
  $convertFromMarkdownString,
  $convertToMarkdownString,
} from '@lexical/mdast';

editor.update(() => $convertFromMarkdownString(source)); // [^id] → cue + note
editor.read(() => $convertToMarkdownString()); // notes → [^id]: … definitions
```

## The syntax

A cue is `[^id]` in the body; its definition is `[^id]: …` on its own line:

```md
Numbers are derived, never stored.[^order]

[^order]: Body cues first, then whatever the notes themselves cite.
```

## Typing a cue

A literal `[^id]` typed into body text also materializes a cue — the same
grammar, applied live — and heals its definition into the section. It is skipped
inside code-formatted text, so an inline `` `[^id]` `` stays literal.

## Where definitions may sit

GFM lets a definition be declared anywhere in the source, not only at the end.
On import they normalize into the one section regardless of where they appeared:

```md
See below.[^a]

[^a]: This definition sat mid-document; it lands in the section all the same.

More body text.
```

Orphan definitions — a `[^id]: …` that nothing cites — are legal in GFM and are
preserved through the round-trip rather than dropped.

## A limitation

Exported ids are the raw identifiers. Ones you wrote by hand survive verbatim;
ones the editor generated export as their internal key, so an inserted note
looks like `[^k3j9x2m1]` in the markdown. Sequential renumbering on export
(`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …) is on the [roadmap](https://github.com/2wheeh/lexical-footnote/blob/main/ROADMAP.md).
